blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 1. Introduction
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Legal, regulatory and especially scientific developments require a revision of biosimilar guidelines, including the overarching Guideline on similar biological medicinal products (CHMP/437/04 Rev.1).
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 2. Problem statement
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The Guideline on similar biological medicinal products (CHMP/437/04 Rev.1) was last revised in 2015. Since then, major progress has been made in the analytical sciences and regulatory field of biosimilars. This is especially evident from the following two developments:
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: The Reflection paper on a tailored clinical approach in biosimilar development | European Medicines Agency (EMA) and initiation of ICH M18 Framework for Determining the Utility of Comparative Efficacy Studies in Biosimilar Development Programs.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: The New Pharmaceutical Legislation (NPL) 1 which will amend the legal-regulatory definition of a biosimilar.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Therefore, the Guideline should be updated to reflect the changing legal, regulatory and scientific landscape.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 3. Discussion (on the problem statement)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The Biosimilar Working Party (BMWP) recommends revising the Guideline on similar biological medicinal products, taking into account the new developments identified above.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The main intention is to provide updated high-level guidance regarding the necessity and utility of Comparative Efficacy Studies (CES) taking into account the scientific considerations reflected in the Reflection paper on a tailored clinical approach in biosimilar development | European Medicines Agency (EMA), the current development of the ICH M18 guideline, and recent regulatory experience obtained with Scientific Advices on biosimilar developments and CHMP decisions on biosimilar marketing authorisation applications (MAAs).
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The guideline also needs to be updated to reflect the new legal definitions and associated high level data requirements for biosimilars in the NPL. In addition, some other parts of the Guideline may need to be reviewed/updated/clarified in light of recent experience.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 4. Recommendation
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The Working Party/Committee recommends revising the Guideline on similar biological medicinal products, taking into account the issues identified above.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In addition, the guideline needs to be updated to reflect the new legal definitions and associated high level data requirements for biosimilars.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Finally, other points may also be amended or clarified based on current experience.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 5. Proposed timetable
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: A three-month consultation period is proposed.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: footnote
blocks.text: 1 The NPL is not yet formally published but the agreed draft subject to final review is available here:
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Concept paper on revision of: Guideline on similar biological medicinal products, The BMWP aims to publish a draft revision of the guideline for consultation in Q2 2027 and to adopt of final document 2028. The main risk for delay arises from the necessity to have thorough discussion/evaluation of the impact of updated definitions in the NPL.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 6. Resource requirements for preparation
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: BMWP will not create a separate drafting group but may set up dedicated subgroups to address specific issues/sections. Regular BMWP meetings will form the basis for the drafting process.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 7. Impact assessment (anticipated)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Since the Reflection paper on a tailored clinical approach in biosimilar development | European Medicines Agency (EMA) has already been published with several regulatory procedures following immediately, the additional scientific impact of the foreseen guideline revision on biosimilar developments is not considered major. However, the guideline needs to be aligned with the reflection paper and is supposed to strengthen the regulatory basis for tailored biosimilar developments. It will also take into account global harmonisation efforts and valuable experience with MAAs for biosimilars without CES.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 8. Interested parties
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: An interested parties meeting is foreseen after publication of the concept paper in order to receive external expert input regarding the guideline revision. Whether further interested parties' meetings will be necessary/helpful will be decided during the revision process.
blocks.speaker: regulator
